append.text: **Ps 89:2 *a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum tu es, Deus* → *desde sempre e para todo o sempre vós sois, Deus*** — copied as the row asked; the Latinist (v1, minor) asked *desde os séculos e até os séculos*, refused for the formula (option `asaeculo`).
**Ps 89:2 *terra et orbis* → *a terra e o mundo*** — applied as D30 names it; no reader remarked.

**Ps 89:3 *Ne avértas hóminem in humilitátem* → *Não desvieis o homem para a humilhação*** (no dative; *in* + accusative) — the ambiguity reader heard moral disgrace as well as lowliness; *reduzais* (MS1932) option. The play *avértas / Convertímini* is lost.
**Ps 89:3 *in humilitátem* → *para a humilhação*; 89:15 *quibus nos humiliásti* → *em que nos humilhastes*** — one family in one psalm, as the row has it.

**Ps 89:5 *quæ pro níhilo habéntur* → *coisas que são tidas por nada*** — the local build (*ter por nada*; æstimári → *ser tido*, D43); the v2 Latinist asked the finite passive (taken) and a masculine *os que* (refused: *quæ* is neuter).

**Ps 89:7, 89:9 (×2) → *desfalecemos … os nossos dias desfaleceram … desfalecemos*** — one verb three times, with days as subject too (the Latin's repetition); the ambiguity reader heard 'our days ran out' rightly but listed *desfalecemos* as unknown. *se acabaram* option.
**Ps 89:7 *in furóre tuo turbáti sumus* → *no vosso furor ficamos perturbados*** — 76:5's build.
**Ps 89:8 *in illuminatióne vultus tui* → *à luz do vosso rosto*** — as foreseen, the v2 Latinist asked *iluminação* (minor); held under this row, as 43:4b.

**Ps 89:9b *Anni nostri sicut aránea meditabúntur* → *Os nossos anos serão meditados como uma aranha*** — the deponent with a passive sense (L&S: late Latin; DRB 'shall be considered', MS1932 *considerados*). Draft 1 had *considerados*; the stylist heard it as report prose and asked *meditados*, which is this row's verb — taken. The ambiguity reader could not see the point of the spider either way (the Latin's crux; no *teia* supplied).

**Ps 89:10 *Si autem in potentátibus* → *Mas, se houver forças*** — the row's 'own word' for strength of years: plural kept, a verb supplied. The v2 Latinist (minor) asked *se nos fortes* (DRB): held — potentátus is power; option.

**Ps 89:10b *supervénit mansuetúdo* → *sobreveio a mansidão*** — the noun as the row foresaw; the ambiguity reader found the clash with *seremos castigados* puzzling (the Latin's own) and listed *sobreveio* as unknown; kept.
**Ps 89:11 *iram tuam dinumeráre* → *contar a vossa ira*** — *sabe* supplied for *novit* + infinitive; the ambiguity reader heard 'tell' first ('count' second) — both are *contar*.

**Ps 89:14 *Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua* → *De manhã fomos cheios da vossa misericórdia*** — the passive of this row, not 62:6's *fartar-se* (the same Greek, ἐμπίμπλημι), because *fartar-se de* is heard as 'be fed up with'. *de manhã* moved to the head (the stylist heard *cheios de manhã* as 'full of morning').
**Ps 89:16 *Réspice in servos tuos, et in ópera tua* → *Olhai para os vossos servos e para as vossas obras*** — the imperative formula.

**Ps 89:16–17 (×3) → *encaminhai*, departing from *endireitai*** — *endireitai os seus filhos* is heard as correcting children; one verb for the Latin's three (*encaminhai os seus filhos … encaminhai sobre nós as obras … e encaminhai a obra*), though the Greek differs (ὁδήγησον / κατεύθυνον). The ambiguity reader heard 'guide' (and 'forward, as a document'). *endireitai* option. Proposes *encaminhar* where the object is persons or works; *endireitar* stays for ways and steps (5:9, 118:133).

terms: | deprecábilis | deixar-se aplacar (*e deixai-vos aplacar para com os vossos servos*) | open | Ps 89:13 only (L&S 'that may be entreated, exorable', citing this verse; παρακλήθητι). MS1932 *Sê exorável* (the exact word, little known) and *sede propício* are options; the ambiguity reader listed *aplacar* as unknown. *super* → *para com* (the v2 Latinist). The link with deprecári → *suplicar* (D35) is lost. |

| sǽculum (a person's lifetime: *sǽculum nostrum*) | *a nossa vida* | open | Ps 89:8 (αἰών ἡμῶν). Draft 1 *o nosso tempo* was heard as a schedule (ambiguity reader); the v1 Latinist asked *vida*, the v2 Latinist asked *tempo* back — the two runs contradict. DRB 'our life'. *idade*, *século* options. Apart from *in sǽculum* (D23). |

| custódia in nocte | *a vigília na noite* (*E como a vigília na noite*) | open | Ps 89:5 (φυλακὴ ἐν νυκτί; MS1932 *vigília da noite*). The ambiguity reader heard a vigil kept, not the watch as a span of time; *guarda* is heard as a person. *como* supplied for *tamquam* of 89:4. |

| prætérire / transíre | *ir-se* (*o dia de ontem, que se foi*) / *passar* (*passe como a erva*) | open | Ps 89:4, 89:6 — two Latin verbs, two Greek (διῆλθεν / παρέλθοι), kept apart so 89:6's own *tránseat … tránseat* is the only *passar*. *que passou* (MS1932) option. |
| aránea | aranha (*como uma aranha*) | open | Ps 89:9b, aligned in v3 with 38:12b *sicut aráneam* → *como uma aranha*, the other place (grep) — no *teia* supplied (MS1932's gloss). |

| herba | erva (*passe como a erva*) | open | Ps 89:6 (χλόη); kept apart from fænum → *feno* (36:2). aréscere → *secar*, décidere → *cair*, indúrare → *endurecer*; the six subjunctives of 89:6 kept (decision `mood6`). |
| splendor | esplendor (*o esplendor do Senhor, nosso Deus*) | open | Ps 89:17 (λαμπρότης); 109:3 *in splendóribus sanctórum* will meet it. |
